Given a $2\times 2$ matrix

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}],
$$

the inverse of $A$ can be found using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{det(A)}[\begin{aligned}d & -b \\ -c & a\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

First, we compute the determinant:

$$
det(A)=6\cdot 1-2\cdot 9=-12
$$

Using the formula, then, the inverse is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{det(A)}[\begin{aligned}d & -b \\ -c & a\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-12}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -9 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1/12 & 1/6 \\ 3/4 & -1/2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can verify the result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A{A}^{-1} & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 9 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1/12 & 1/6 \\ 3/4 & -1/2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}\,✓ \\ {A}^{-1}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1/12 & 1/6 \\ 3/4 & -1/2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 9 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
